subject: microbiology
title: HBV Window Period, Dane Particle, HBV DNA and Hepatitis C

steps.tx: The HBV **window period** is the interval when HBsAg has disappeared but anti-HBs has not yet become detectable. **Anti-HBc IgM** can be the only positive marker during this gap in acute resolving infection. HBV DNA may also clarify occult or early disease. The window is a sequence problem, not a separate species of hepatitis, and timing plus the full marker panel resolves it.
steps.say: In the HBV window, anti-HBc IgM is the footprint between antigen loss and antibody arrival.

left.title: Marker sequence
points: HBsAg rises then falls in recovery
Anti HBs appears last and protects

right.title: Window findings
points: Anti HBc IgM positive in acute recovery
HBV DNA may still be low positive

steps.tx: The **Dane particle** contains an envelope with HBsAg, a nucleocapsid with HBcAg and partially double-stranded DNA plus polymerase. Excess subviral HBsAg particles are not infectious. The virus uses reverse transcription despite carrying DNA, making polymerase the tenofovir and entecavir target class. HBV DNA level informs infectivity, phase classification, treatment need and mother-to-child prevention decisions.
steps.say: HBV DNA is the direct measure of the infectious Dane particle's replication.

right.title: HBV DNA uses
points: High maternal load guides perinatal prophylaxis strategy

steps.tx: **Hepatitis C virus** is an enveloped positive-sense RNA flavivirus transmitted mainly by blood. Acute infection is often silent, yet most untreated people historically developed chronic infection, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma risk. Anti-HCV indicates exposure but cannot separate resolved from active infection; HCV RNA confirms current viraemia and is required before direct-acting antiviral treatment.
steps.say: Anti HCV is the exposure scar; HCV RNA proves living infection.

right.title: RNA positive
points: Quantify before treatment in many pathways
Genotype less universally needed with pangenotypic regimens
Confirm cure with sustained virologic response

steps.tx: HCV has multiple **genotypes** and subtypes shaped by its error-prone RNA polymerase. Genotype once dictated regimen and duration; pangenotypic direct-acting antivirals have simplified most care, though genotype 3, cirrhosis and prior failure still matter in selected pathways. Resistance testing is not routine before first therapy in many patients but becomes important after direct-acting antiviral failure.
steps.say: Pangenotypic therapy reduced genotype's power, but prior failure restores its importance.

left.title: Genotype legacy
points: Early direct antivirals were genotype specific
Genotype 3 linked with steatosis and harder cure historically
Subtype matters in some resistance patterns

steps.tx: **Sustained virologic response** means HCV RNA remains undetectable usually twelve weeks after therapy and is regarded as cure. It greatly reduces liver complications but does not erase established cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance needs, nor does it prevent reinfection. Patients with ongoing exposure require harm reduction and repeat RNA testing when risk continues, because antibody remains positive and is useless for reinfection detection.
steps.say: SVR cures HCV infection, not cirrhosis risk already built or future exposure risk.

steps.tx: A common examination trap is calling **anti-HCV positive** synonymous with immunity. It is not protective and may coexist with high-level viraemia. Likewise, a negative antibody test in very early infection or severe immunosuppression does not always exclude HCV; RNA testing closes those windows. Distinguishing exposure markers from nucleic acid markers is the shared skill across HBV, HCV and HIV testing.
steps.say: For blood-borne viruses, antibody tells exposure, nucleic acid tells current replication.

left.title: Antibody answers
points: Has the immune system met it
HBV anti HBs can mean protection
HIV antibody is part of diagnostic algorithm

right.title: Nucleic acid answers
points: Useful in early and occult infection
Used to prove HCV cure and monitor HIV or HBV
